packages.description: Replicates layout of one hierarchical sheet to other copies of the same sheet.
packages.description_full:
Replicate layout of one hierarchical sheet to other hierarchical sheets. The replication is based upon hierarchical sheets in eeschema. The basic requirement for replication is that the section to be replicated (source) is completely contained within a single hierarchical sheet, and replicated sections (destination) are just copies of the same sheet. Complex hierarchies are supported therefore replicated sheet can contain subsheets. The plugin replicates footprints, zones, tracks, text and drawings.
After the section for replication (source section) has been laid out (footprints, tracks, text objects and zones placed) you need to:
1. Place the anchor footprints for the destiantion sections you want to replicate. This defines the position and orientation of replicated sections. You can use PlaceFootprints action plugin for this.
2. Select the same anchor footprint within the source section.
3. Run the plugin.
4. Choose which hierarchical level you wish to replicate.
5. Select which sheets you want to replicate (default is all of them)
6. Select whether you want to replicate also tracks, zones and/or text objects.
7. Select whether you want to replicate tracks/zones/text which intersect the pivot bounding box or just those contained within the bounding box.
8. Select whether you want to delete already laid out tracks/zones/text (this is useful when updating an already replicated layout).
9. Hit OK.
By default, only objects which are fully contained in the bounding box constituted by all the footprints in the section will be replicated. You can select to also replicate zones and tracks which intersect this bounding box. Additionally, tracks, text and zones which are already laid out in the replicated bounding boxes can be removed (useful when updating). Note that bounding boxes are squares aligned with the x and y axis, regardless of section orientation.
packages.name: Replicate Layout

packages.description: Multi-Scope PCB Assembly Variants
packages.description_full:
KiVar provides multi-aspect PCB assembly variant and micro-variant selection.
It assigns component values, field content, footprint attributes (such as 'Do not populate') and features (e.g. solder paste application or individual 3D model visibility) according to variation rules specified in component fields.
— Key Concepts —
• Designs may contain multiple independent variation aspects (micro-variants).
• Variation rules are fully contained in the native design files (no external files required) and portable (copying parts to another design keeps variation specification intact).
• Component data is modified in place, enabling compatibility with any exporter.
• No external state information is stored; currently matching variation choices are detected automatically.
• Optional external variant definition table in independent file format (CSV) enables switching of aspect groups based on a single variant name.
— Documentation and Demo Project —
The variation expression syntax and variant table format specification including examples can be found under the 'Documentation' resource link.
A demo KiCad project is contained in the source code repository, which can be downloaded as an archive from the 'Source and Demo' resource link.
— Support —
If you find bugs or want to discuss ideas or questions, please follow the 'Issue Tracker' resource link.

packages.description: Copy a project's external symbols, footprints and 3D models into local libraries so it opens on any machine. IPC-based (KiCad 10+) and reversible.
packages.description_full:
Makes a KiCad project self-contained. It copies the external symbols, footprints, and 3D models a project uses into project-local libraries and updates every reference, so the schematic, board, 3D view, and STEP export still work on any machine even when the original global or third-party libraries aren't installed.

- It handles symbols, footprints, and 3D models, not only one of them. You can localize any combination in a single pass.
- It uses the IPC API (kicad-python / kipy), so it runs on KiCad 10 and keeps running on KiCad 11 and later, where the old SWIG bindings are gone.
- Revert is exact. Each file is backed up before it is touched, and one click puts the project back the way it was and removes the local copies.
- You can localize just the parts you want.
- Ticking 'include standard KiCad libraries' also pulls in the stock libs, so the project depends on nothing installed globally.

The plugin connects over IPC only to locate the open project, then edits the project files on disk with a small S-expression parser that rewrites only the references it needs and leaves every other byte alone.

To use, save the project, run the plugin, then reopen it in KiCad to pick up the changes.

packages.description: Generate complete PCB manufacturing files from KiCad with one click.
packages.description_full:
The AIVON Production Toolkit simplifies the PCB production file preparation process by automatically exporting all required manufacturing documents from your KiCad project and saving them locally.

Export the following production files with one click:

- Gerber files in the correct format for PCB fabrication.
- IPC-Netlist file for manufacturing verification.
- BOM file containing component information for assembly.
- Pick and Place file for SMT assembly.

All exported files are organized into a complete production package, ready to be shared with your PCB manufacturer or used for manufacturing review.

About AIVON:
AIVON provides PCB fabrication and PCB assembly services for engineers, startups, and hardware companies worldwide. Our manufacturing capabilities include multilayer PCBs, HDI, flexible PCBs, rigid-flex PCBs, aluminum PCBs, and turnkey PCB assembly.
The AIVON Production Toolkit helps engineers streamline the transition from PCB design to manufacturing by reducing repetitive export steps and ensuring production files are prepared consistently.
packages.name: AIVON Production Toolkit

packages.description: Export manufacturing files and send your PCB project to AIVON for fast online quotation.
packages.description_full:
Send your KiCad project to AIVON with one click for PCB fabrication and PCB assembly quotation.
The plugin automatically exports the manufacturing data required for production, eliminating manual file preparation and reducing the risk of missing or incorrect files.
When you click AIVON Plug-in button, the plugin generates:

- Gerber files in the right format for PCB fabrication
- IPC Netlist file
- BOM-file, including all information of components
- Pick and Place-file for PCBA

After the export is complete, your project can be uploaded directly to AIVON for an instant online quotation. The uploaded data is organized as a manufacturing package, allowing our engineering team to perform a Design for Manufacturing (DFM) review before production.
If you update your PCB design, simply export again to create a new manufacturing package based on the latest project revision.

About AIVON:
AIVON is an online PCB manufacturing platform providing PCB fabrication and turnkey PCB assembly services for engineers and hardware teams worldwide. From prototype to volume production, AIVON supports rigid PCBs, HDI, flexible PCBs, rigid-flex PCBs, aluminum PCBs, and complete PCB assembly, helping streamline the journey from design to manufacturing.
packages.name: AIVON Plug-in for KiCad

packages.description: Create PCB labels, symbols, component callouts, header overlays, QR Codes, and barcodes inside KiCad
packages.description_full: Kobee Studio creates editable PCB artwork on silkscreen, copper, and solder-mask layers. It includes parametric labels with optional underlines, PCB symbols, searchable presets, custom SVG uploads, icon and quick-label visibility controls, saved profiles, mm and mil display units, component callouts and arrays, configurable 2.54 mm header overlays, QR Codes, Code 128 barcodes, and optional readable text beneath machine codes. Kobee Studio evolved from KiBuzzard and now provides a modern KiCad 10 IPC workflow for creating consistent PCB graphics.
packages.name: Kobee Studio

packages.description: Generate an annotated pinout image from the active board.
packages.description_full: Pinout Image Generator extracts pad positions, net names and net classes from the currently-open board and produces a coloured pinout diagram overlaid on a top-view render. Labels and function categories can be fully edited before rendering. A separate CLI and Tkinter GUI are also available for workflows that start from a gerber F.Mask SVG and a custom PNG.
packages.name: Pinout Image Generator

packages.description: Automate escape routing (fanout) for dense IC packages like QFN, QFP, and BGA
packages.description_full: A powerful Python-based plugin to automate escape routing (fanout) for dense IC packages like SOIC, QFN, QFP, and BGA in KiCad. It features advanced 3-segment routing algorithms, staggered alignments, and full parameter control to generate clean, DRC-error-free tracks and vias instantly.
packages.name: Fanout Tool

packages.description: Checks your design and refuses to ship a fab package with errors it already knows about.
packages.description_full:
prefab-gate runs kicad-cli DRC with zone refill and schematic parity checking, classifies every finding as blocking or cosmetic, and reports whether the board is fit to fabricate.

The toolbar button checks and reports. It never writes to your project: the check runs against a copy of the board, schematic, project and custom-rules files in a temporary directory, because DRC refills zones and would otherwise rewrite the board open in your editor.

Stale zone fills are reported rather than silently repaired, and the dialog always names the file it read and when it was last saved, because unsaved editor changes cannot be detected reliably from a plugin.

Exporting a verified fab package - gerbers, drill, CPL and BOM, with a manifest pinning them to the board that was checked - is available from the command line version.
packages.name: prefab-gate

packages.description: Footprints used by Kikakuka for couplers, variables, and string templates.
packages.description_full: A KiCad footprint library for Kikakuka workflows. It provides the CouplerFixed, CouplerMoving, and CouplerAt footprints used by FreekiCAD assembly alignment, plus Variable and StringTemplate footprints used by the Fabrication Planner.
packages.name: Kikakuka Footprints

packages.description: Copy repeated-circuit placement and project-local footprint edits with explicit PCB selection. English and Turkish UI.
packages.description_full: Layout Clone has separate Placement and Footprint Edits tabs. Copy anchor-relative placements to explicitly selected PCB targets using connectivity matching, or explicitly choose Placement only for groups with different wiring. Placement only matches type, value, footprint and pad numbers without claiming electrical equivalence; it preserves target pad nets and never infers terminal swaps from nets. Padless logos, text and graphics are excluded from the component model, while duplicate references on pad-bearing components remain blocked. Placement supports mixed front/back groups. Footprint Edits copies project-local pad geometry, graphics and complete 3D model settings while preserving target position, angle, side, identity, schematic linkage and pad nets. Includes explicit previews, ambiguous-part choices, English/Turkish UI and native undo. No library or schematic changes; no auto-save. Windows / KiCad 10.0 testing release. Close other PCB and schematic editors before applying. See the bundled usage notes.
packages.name: Layout Clone

packages.description: KiCad 10 IPC plugin for inspecting PCB holes by drill size or net and quickly locating pads and vias.
packages.description_full: HoleFinder groups all drilled objects by drill size or net, shows the corresponding pads and vias, and lets you quickly locate a selected object on the PCB. The view is centered on the object and the object briefly blinks to make it easy to spot.
packages.name: HoleFinder

packages.description: Manage part data using an http library
packages.description_full: This plugin utilizes the new KiCad http library and extends it with a web component to manage part data like part number, manufacturer, distributor order number. It requires an Instance of https://heronitec-solutions.github.io/KiComLibServer/ .
packages.name: KiComLib Client

packages.description: Simulations for routed boards: net check, TDR wave animation, Monte Carlo yield, plane slot 2D. UI: English, Deutsch, 中文.
packages.description_full: A KiCad 10 plugin (IPC API) that analyses the routed board. Net check: length, layer changes, 90 degree corners and differential pair length skew from the real tracks. Wave / TDR: 1D lossless transmission line animation (MP4) using Z0 from a 2D field solver. Monte Carlo: Z0 spread and yield over typical manufacturing tolerances. Plane slot: 2D plane-pair FDTD and DC current spreading around a slot in the reference plane. All local and free. Model limits are stated in the plugin: the simulations are simplified and qualitative, with no stub, via or crosstalk model yet, and they do not replace a 3D full-wave solver such as openEMS. UI languages: English (default), Deutsch, 中文.
packages.name: Z0 Wavelab

packages.description: Local 2D field solver: read the stackup, solve track width and gap for a target impedance (single-ended and differential), write net classes and design rules, check routed tracks. UI: English, Deutsch, 中文.
packages.description_full: A KiCad 10 plugin (IPC API) that takes the board stackup and a target impedance and computes the track geometry with a real 2D field solver (Laplace equation, Gauss integral). Everything runs locally and is free. Results: track width for Z0, and width and gap for Zdiff, per copper layer. They are written into net classes (these steer the router) and optionally as custom design rules (.kicad_dru) for DRC. It also copies a table for the KiCad Tuning Profile dialog and checks already routed tracks against the target. Stackups can be edited and saved; fab presets come from published stackups. UI languages: English (default), Deutsch, 中文. Accuracy is typically within a few percent against reference cases and is not a substitute for the fab's own impedance report. The KiCad API cannot write the stackup or tuning profile geometry, so those steps stay manual.
packages.name: Z0 Field Solver

packages.description: Autoroute the open board: exact-geometry (shape) or grid engine, any number of copper layers.
packages.description_full:
Tracklayer routes the unrouted nets of the open board and adds the tracks and vias as one undoable change, then refills the zones. The shape engine works on exact geometry: every obstacle is grown by the clearance plus half the track width and tracks run corner to corner, so clearances are met exactly and tight escapes from fine-pitch pads just work. The grid engine gives classic 45-degree tracks. Net classes, locked and hand-routed copper, keep-outs and pours are respected. Any number of copper layers with through vias.

Tools > External Plugins > Tracklayer autoroute. Pure Python. Runs through the KiCad API: enable it once under Preferences > Plugins > Enable KiCad API.

Made by Tiggy Engineering (www.tiggyengineering.com). Free and open source; if it saves you an evening, have a look at what we make, or buy us a beer through GitHub Sponsors: github.com/sponsors/MichaelGaylor
packages.name: Tracklayer autorouter

packages.description: Signal paths, PCB tools and deterministic manufacturing packages for KiCad 10
packages.description_full: TraceForge combines signal path timing, trace cleanup, rounded track corners, exact-angle component rotation, via stitching, via array placement, RF via fencing, BGA fanout and live net visualization in one PCB Editor panel. The Manufacturing tab reviews saved projects, runs KiCad checks and builds PCBWay or PCBPower deliverable packages from verified choices. Toolbar and Tools menu shortcuts open its feature tabs directly. PCB editing reads the live board through KiCad 10's pcbnew bindings. Manufacturing export uses kicad-cli and a separate Python with openpyxl. Supports Windows and KiCad 10 only. See the project homepage for documentation and known limits.
packages.name: TraceForge

packages.description: Fill a selected copper zone with a configurable pattern of stitching vias.
packages.description_full: ViaStitcher is a KiCad PCB Editor action plugin that fills a selected copper zone with a configurable grid of vias. It supports spacing and offset controls, clearance checks, randomized placement, filled-copper validation, and selective removal of vias previously created by the plugin.
packages.name: ViaStitcher

packages.description: Component sourcing, schematic metadata editing, datasheets, and semantic netlist checks.
packages.description_full:
traces opens from the KiCad PCB Editor and works with the project's schematic. Source components from JLCPCB/LCSC, Digi-Key, and Mouser, edit component properties, import symbols and footprints, and run semantic netlist checks.

Requires a separately installed local traces server, Python 3.11+, uv, and Node.js 20+. Start the server before opening the plugin. Inference uses either local Ollama or your OpenRouter API key; supplier requests use external services. Some suppliers require your own API keys. No traces account is required.

This initial PCM release targets KiCad 10 on macOS and is marked testing. See the installation guide for backend setup and migration from a manually installed plugin.
packages.name: traces

packages.description: Obsidian-style notes inside KiCad
packages.description_full: KiSidian is a KiCad plugin for writing and organizing engineering notes directly inside PCB projects. It features a split-pane Markdown editor with live preview, dark mode, and project-relative storage.
packages.name: KiSidian

packages.description: Compute the VSWR, efficiency and gain of a PCB antenna. Needs LW RF Studio, a separate download.
packages.description_full:
Before you use this plugin, download and install LW RF Studio on the same PC from https://lwtech.org/#download

The plugin does not work without it: it runs every computation with LW RF Studio and the openEMS solver that its setup installs.

LW Antenna Check computes the VSWR of the antenna on the open KiCad board and, with the Accurate speed, its efficiency and gain. These computations are free. Full analysis (Smith chart, 3D pattern, currents, matching, import) is in LW RF Studio.
packages.name: LW Antenna Check

packages.description: Check your board for small mistakes before you order it: mismatched part numbers, out-of-stock JLCPCB parts, LEDs with no resistor. Free, offline.
packages.description_full:
Catch small PCB mistakes before you order.

Click Check design and in about a second you get a short list of things to double-check, each with the reason and a suggested fix:
- part numbers that don't match the part's value or size (with the optional JLCPCB parts list)
- parts out of stock at JLCPCB (optional live lookup)
- the same value written two ways
- an LED with no resistor, I2C pull-up problems, labels that should connect but don't

On one open-source board it found 48 capacitors labelled "10u" that all had the part number of a 1 µF part.

It only reads your board. No account, no API key, no internet needed for the check.

How much to trust it: it's a first pass, not a full design review. On 12 boards it had never seen, 44% of its warnings were judged correct (by AI reviewers, not human engineers). Treat findings as things to double-check.

Also included: a router for small boards. The route is shown as a preview, KiCad's DRC checks it, and one Undo reverts it. One track width for all nets; no differential pairs or length matching.

Alpha. KiCad 10, tested on Windows only. MIT licence.

Setup: during the install KiCad asks to enable the KiCad API; click Yes. The first start installs about 300 MB of Python packages (about 4 minutes in our test), then the VelaTrace button appears.
packages.name: VelaTrace

packages.description: One-click Eagle (.sch/.brd) to KiCad 10 import with KiCad's own importer, automatic repair and strict QC against the Eagle source and Gerbers.
packages.description_full:
Eagle Exhumer brings old Autodesk EAGLE designs (6.x-9.x XML .sch/.brd, and binary 4.x/5.x files through a built-in converter) into KiCad 10.

One click: pick the Eagle .sch or .brd, and KiCad's own EAGLE importer runs first. Eagle Exhumer then repairs automatically what the import leaves broken, from defects found on real boards: power nets, Eagle 'nc' pins, lost net names, package copper polygons and printed jumpers (net ties), NPTH rings, via restring, net classes and the Eagle clearance matrix, milling, board outlines drawn inside packages, copper layer count, and more.

Every conversion ends with a strong quality control against the Eagle source and the Eagle manufacturing Gerbers, with a strict PASS / FAIL verdict, a Markdown report and 3D renders.

Nothing is deleted without your approval: every proposed removal is shown with a before/after picture and applied only if you tick it.

Windows: one-click import of a new design. All platforms: fix + check of an already imported project (Linux/macOS: experimental).

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Autodesk. EAGLE is a trademark of Autodesk, Inc.
packages.name: Eagle Exhumer

packages.description: Interactive multilayer DC current, voltage-drop and estimated board-temperature maps. Local KiCad 10 analysis.
packages.description_full: A free local analysis plugin for KiCad 10. Click pads or copper in a saved PCB view to define voltage sources, current loads and component heat. Includes filled copper zones, tracks, pads, via spans, multilayer DC distribution and coupled steady-state board temperature estimates. Inspect temperature, current density and voltage-drop overlays by layer and net without changing the coupled model. Includes English/Turkish UI, grouped contacts, visibility controls, saved scenarios, generic material settings and isolated read-only analysis snapshots. NumPy and wxPython must already be available in the tested Windows KiCad installation. No account, network access, subscription or downloaded solver is used. Engineering prototype: requires mesh-refinement checks and independent measurements. Does not model semiconductor junction temperature, switching losses automatically, airflow CFD, radiation, heatsinks or thermal-interface materials. Not a certified ampacity calculator. Windows / KiCad 10.0 SWIG testing release.
packages.name: PCB Heatmap

packages.description: Place WS2812 / SMD LEDs as a 2D grid inside a shape from an SVG, PNG or BMP image, with schematic, PCB and LED map export.
packages.description_full:
AutoLED fills a shape taken from an SVG, PNG, BMP or JPG image with a 2D grid of LEDs such as WS2812B, WS2812B-2020, SK6812MINI, 0805, 0603 or 1206.

The image is converted to black and white with a configurable threshold, scaled by width, height, percent or DPI, and LEDs are placed with a configurable pitch, border offset and grid shift, optionally keeping the whole LED body inside the shape. A live preview (zoom and pan) shows LEDs, decoupling capacitors, connectors and the data chain.

Outputs:
- the LED map as JSON, TXT and a C/C++ header (mask, chain index, row/column tables)
- a schematic: WS2812 daisy chain with decoupling caps and in/out connectors, or a row/column matrix for simple LEDs
- footprints placed on the PCB with nets, in a group that can be regenerated
- an optional board outline or cut line that follows the image shape (also exported as SVG and DXF)
- optional autorouting with Freerouting (requires Java and the Freerouting jar, e.g. from the Freerouting plugin)

Chain order: rows or columns, zigzag, start corner, optional 180 degree rotation of LEDs on backward lines. Capacitor rotation / position and connector footprint, pin order, placement and side are configurable.
packages.name: AutoLED

packages.description: Signal and power integrity checks: opens the board in kisi's viewer in the browser.
packages.description_full:
kisi checks signal and power integrity of a KiCad board: trace impedance per net class, high-speed channels against interface profiles (loss, eye, skew), vias, crosstalk, the regulator chain, DC voltage drop and PDN impedance.

The toolbar button opens the board of the PCB editor in kisi's viewer, a self-contained page that runs offline in the default browser. The board's <board>.kisi.json (values with sources that the board file lacks) is loaded with it, or created as an empty skeleton next to the board. The viewer's Prepare PCB page fills and saves it.

The plugin reads the saved board file; it never writes KiCad's files. Needs the KiCad API (Preferences > Plugins > Enable KiCad API); KiCad installs kicad-python on first start.
packages.name: kisi – SI/PI checks

packages.description: Split a power layer into one continuous zone per net
packages.description_full: On a board where several supplies share one inner power layer, kicad-splitplane computes exactly one continuous copper zone per net from the positions of its vias and through-hole pads, keeps foreign vias out of every zone and writes the zones into the open board as a single undo step. A preview shows the split before anything is written.
packages.name: kicad-splitplane

packages.description: Power Integrity Simulator: DC drop, AC PDN impedance over frequency, and PSU coupled noise, with 3D visualization of the board's real copper.
packages.description_full:
KiPI is a power integrity analyzer for KiCad boards.

DC: IR drop, current density with flow arrows, via and pad currents, and copper temperature from Joule heating, shown in 3D on the board's real copper.

AC: PDN impedance over frequency at each load, against its target impedance, with the board's planes, vias, decoupling capacitors (SPICE or S-parameter models) and VRMs.

KiPI installs its Python dependencies (NumPy, SciPy, PySide6, PyVista and others, about 250 MB) into the plugin's environment the first time it starts. It also runs on its own, with a launcher, and imports boards from other layout tools.
packages.name: KiPI

packages.description: Generate Gerbers, drill files, BOM, position file, IPC-D-356 netlist, and interactive BOM in one click.
packages.description_full: LionCircuits adds a single toolbar button to the PCB Editor. Clicking it exports Gerbers and Excellon drill files (LionCircuits' fab-ready naming standard), a BOM for assembly, a BOM for components (supplier quote/procurement), a component position (CPL) file, an IPC-D-356 bare-board test netlist, and an interactive HTML BOM (using InteractiveHtmlBom if installed, otherwise a built-in fallback table). Gerbers and drill files are optionally zipped into a fab-ready package.
packages.name: LionCircuits Fabrication Export

packages.description: DRC-first adaptive via stitching: grid plus gap-only refinement, power-plane protection, drafts to approve before placing.
packages.description_full:
Adaptive via stitching for any net (GND by default). Named after the Italian pasta colander (colino): it perforates the ground planes like one, and keeps the RF in.

- Classic stitching grid (default 200 mil), then refinement at half and quarter pitch only inside the gaps that are still uncovered.
- Every candidate passes an exact geometry gate: zone fill on every layer, hole-to-hole, pads, keepouts, courtyards, clearance to foreign copper. Optional KiCad DRC after placing removes any offending new via.
- Other-net planes (power pours) are detected; per plane you choose forbid (default), base grid only, or allow. The proposal image marks restricted planes and every via that would perforate one.
- Drafts (A/B/C) with a coverage map and an empty-board benchmark are shown before anything is placed; placing is one Undo step and all new vias go into one group that can be removed with one click.
- Connectivity rescue: the fewest vias that reconnect isolated copper islands of the net, preferring spots that perforate no plane.
- mil or mm units.
packages.name: Z2 Via Colino

packages.description: Fillets at the corners of T-junctions between tracks
packages.description_full: KiCad only adds a track-to-track teardrop where the width changes. This plugin fills the corners of every T-junction (same net and layer, away from pads and vias) with copper, one T-td zone per corner.
packages.name: T-Junction Teardrops

packages.description: EM simulation of PCBs in KiCad: ports, stackup, mesh preview, S-parameters, currents and voltages on the board (openEMS-based).
packages.description_full:
Electromagnetic (FDTD) simulation of the open board from inside the PCB editor.

- Ports as a + pad and its ground reference (connector GND pads, IC GND pins or the plane below), picked from the PCB editor selection and drawn as markers on a user layer (no DRC/ERC impact).
- Fab stackup presets (JLCPCB 2-layer and 4-layer, own JSON).
- Mesh preview on a user layer with cell count and run-time estimate.
- Simulate: S-parameters (Touchstone), line impedance and effective permittivity, 3D viewer.
- Fields of every run, scaled to 1 W: surface current maps with current lines and layer voltages with iso-voltage lines on the board; a 3D viewer with arrows, phase animation and E-field cut planes.
- Two-pad R/L/C footprints are simulated as lumped elements.

The solver is the Z2 EMS engine (openEMS with a CUDA engine, conformal metal edges and a KiCad importer, GPL-3.0). It is a separate download of about 160 MB: on Windows the plugin offers to download and install it on first use (from github.com/z2labs/z2ems/releases, SHA-256 checked); on Linux and macOS it is built from source and the plugin is pointed to its folder.

Requires KiCad 10 with the IPC API server enabled (Preferences > Plugins).
packages.name: Z2Labs EMS

packages.description: Vulkan GPU + Multithreaded CPU Auto-Placer and Auto-Router for KiCad
packages.description_full: Vulcan's Trials combines schematic-aware Parallel Tempering Simulated Annealing auto-placement with a Vulkan GPU-accelerated, negotiated-congestion, dynamic-nudge multi-layer autorouter.
packages.name: Vulcan's Trials
